question: The coarse and medium meshes differ by 21-24 drag counts. WHERE?
method: Per-cell pressure drag from the surface solutions, -cp*(areaVec . dragDir)/area_ref. Validated against each run's recorded CDp: exact to 0.000 counts at alpha 0 and 0.05 at alpha 4, the residual being the tip-cap zone which is excluded.
runs: g83, g47, g13 at gci_C and gci_M, alpha 0/4/8

spanwise_dCDp_counts.reading: roughly in proportion to area, so this is a chordwise error spread over the wing, not a tip or wake effect

rms_dcp.reading: with incidence the disagreement migrates from the lower surface to the upper

cell_aspect_ratio.reading: uniform refinement preserves cell SHAPE and changes only cell SIZE, which is the control confirming the gci_C -> gci_M difference is resolution and not a shape artefact

findings: The last 5 % of chord gives -9.2 to -10.3 counts in ALL SIX cases -- three wings, two incidences, a spread of barely one count. That band alone is 40-45 % of the total difference.
The first 5 % gives a further -4.5 to -15.5 counts, more variable between geometries.
The mid-chord 20-60 %, which is 40 % of the surface, contributes +/-2 counts.
So the error is an EDGE problem, not a chordwise-resolution problem. Refining the whole chord works because it also refines the edges.
This independently supports family 2's edges=True. It was added on a 7 % argument from gci_C_edge; this decomposition says the edges carry closer to 80 %.
The spanwise distribution follows area, which is another independent line against the wake hypothesis retracted on 2026-09-24.
cheapest_next_test: Hold every count fixed and refine ONLY ds_te_frac. If the trailing-edge band is the mechanism it should recover most of 10 counts for almost no cells.

correction_2026_09_24.what_was_wrong: Reported as 'the last 5 % of chord carries 10 of the 22 counts', which reads as a trailing-edge boundary-layer effect. Binning by chord fraction lumps the blunt base face in with the surface approaching it.
correction_2026_09_24.how_it_was_found: Challenged on the grounds that the LEADING edge was believed to be the issue. Re-split the surface by GEOMETRY -- the base is every cell whose outward normal has n_x > 0.7 -- instead of by chord fraction.
correction_2026_09_24.direction_check: Verified first that min-x IS the leading edge at every spanwise station, against the built planform: g83 LE x 0.0000 / TE x 0.8673, g47 0.0000 / 0.7057, g13 0.0000 / 1.0884. The chordwise sense was correct.

geometry_confound_tested_and_ruled_out.worry: ds_te_frac scales with the family (0.00100 -> 0.00077), so the base might be a different SHAPE between levels, making this a geometry sweep rather than a grid study.
geometry_confound_tested_and_ruled_out.measurement: base height / chord at the root, measured on the built meshes: gci_C 0.002499, gci_M 0.002499, ratio 1.0000 on both g83 and g13.
geometry_confound_tested_and_ruled_out.conclusion: Identical geometry. ds_te_frac sets the NODE SPACING at the trailing-edge corners, not the base opening. The -10 counts is pure resolution: 3 interior nodes across the base at gci_C against 5 at gci_M.

correction_2026_09_24.corrected_finding: Two distinct errors, not one. (1) The BLUNT BASE FACE, 0.25 % of the wetted area, gives -9.8 to -11.0 counts in every case -- a spread of 1.2 counts across three wings and two incidences. Base drag nearly halves, 22.4-25.2 -> 12.6-14.2, because the coarse mesh predicts a more negative base pressure. (2) The LEADING EDGE gives more in total, -4.5 to -15.5, but is highly variable: its two sub-bands partly cancel and the split between them swings 24 counts between cases. The trailing-edge SURFACE contributes essentially nothing.
correction_2026_09_24.relation_to_the_earlier_LE_finding: The earlier '+11.17 counts in one spanwise band at the leading edge' came from the WALL-NORMAL refinement test, a different comparison. It does not conflict with this one.
correction_2026_09_24.revised_cheapest_test: Hold every count fixed and raise ONLY n_base, the node count across the blunt face, from 5 to 7. That is a handful of cells on 0.25 % of the wetted area. If the base is the mechanism it should recover most of 10 counts for almost nothing.
